prize_parts.citation: for the invention and development of the optical lattice clock, in which atoms trapped at the magic wavelength brought the measurement of time to the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: I change my preferred configuration from B032 to B056. My test is whether we have found the original experiment and are absolutely sure of the people who did it. For the lattice clock the record is short and the chain is visible: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength condition and made the first demonstrations with strontium, and Ye's group took the scheme to the accuracy and stability frontier, linked it to the comb and showed what it can measure. The result has been reproduced and surpassed independently at JILA, RIKEN and Tokyo, PTB, NIST and SYRTE, and it already gives answers about nature: gravitational redshift across millimetres, limits on the constancy of constants and dark-matter couplings. It is the only shortlisted candidate that all eight of us ranked, with one pair of names proposed by everyone. That breadth does not replace the science, but it tells me the credit question has been answered the same way eight times. Citing the lattice scheme and the 10^-18 performance keeps it clearly apart from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize.
statement.case_against: It is still an invention and a measurement capability rather than a new phenomenon, and the committee has twice recognised the tools it rests on, the comb in 2005 and single-ion control in 2012. Two names cannot cover Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley, Bloom and the PTB, NIST and SYRTE groups, who made real contributions to accuracy and stability. The redefinition of the second has not yet happened, so a sceptic can argue for waiting. I also note that my case for B056 is the same kind of argument I made for B032, an instrument that opens a door, so I cannot dismiss it as metrology without dismissing my own earlier choice.

responses.point: Kroll asks that the citation be written narrowly around the many-atom neutral lattice scheme, so that the committee is not seen as recognising timekeeping twice, and says he would accept B032 as an alternative if the clock stalls. He also stresses that Krivanek's STEM corrector is a real omission.
responses.response: I accept his wording point and have written my citation around the lattice clock and the 10^-18 performance. On B032, I reread the history of Krivanek's and Batson's STEM corrector and I can no longer say that the TEM line of Rose, Haider and Urban is the only original achievement. A three-name limit cannot do justice to both, and I am not sure the primary record lets us choose between them. That is why I move away from my own field and keep B032 only as an alternative. I also thank him for the point that the ion-clock overlap is answered by the neutral-atom many-body scheme, which is a different achievement from single-ion control.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that the comb is the tool that reads out a lattice clock and not the clock itself, and that the 1e-18 regime with a magic-wavelength lattice is a separate achievement from 2005 and 2012. She also says the redefinition of the second is a consequence and not a precondition.
responses.response: This answers the question that I raised against myself in round 1. If the comb prize was for the ruler and the ion prize for control of a single quantum system, then holding thousands of neutral atoms without perturbing the transition is a different invention, and I find it convincing. I also agree that the redefinition is a consequence: the original experiments and the independent confirmation are already in the record, which is the evidence I ask for. I would still ask you and Kroll, as the atomic physicists, to name in the committee text which results beyond accuracy, such as the redshift measurement and the constants limits, carry the claim to being a statement about nature.

responses.point: Mehlig keeps topological insulators first and says B032 is only his second alternative. He also asks whether the clock is a new principle or a superb realisation of a known one.
responses.response: I share his hesitation on principle and my answer is the magic-wavelength condition, which is a new idea and not a refinement, because it removes the dominant systematic while keeping a large atom number. On B007, my round-1 concern about the credit chain has not gone away. The HgTe observation followed a proposal by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who are not credited, so the experiment confirms a prediction by people outside the trio, and the 3D ARPES work is also outside it. I would be glad to see topological insulators on a later shortlist, but I cannot see a defensible three-name credit this year, and the clock needs no such compromise.

responses.point: Pearce, our chair, now ranks B056 first and notes that it could bridge members who favour topology and those who favour precision measurement. He also withdraws some of his support for IceCube because of attribution and source identification.
responses.response: I agree with his reasons for moving and I have moved too. On the Wolf Prize point that I raised against his reading of B032, I stay with my position that it is not evidence of original work. His response on IceCube strengthens my own view that B003 should remain an alternative, since the diffuse flux is established but AMANDA, DUMAND and the source population make a two-name credit hard to defend this year.

uncertainties: Whether Katori and Ye are the fairest two names given the parallel strontium-clock work at SYRTE, PTB and NIST, which cannot fit within the three-person limit.
Whether the committee wants to wait for the redefinition of the second, which I judge unnecessary because the confirmation is already in the record.
Whether the primary record on priority between the Rose, Haider and Urban correctors and the Nion STEM corrector supports a three-name credit in a later year.
Whether my own field closeness to B032 has biased how strongly I argued for it in round 1, and whether I have now overcorrected.
statement.conflict_note: My first-round flag on B032 stands: it is in my field of transmission electron microscopy and I know the community through IFSM, though my profile lists no direct collaboration with Rose, Haider, Urban or Krivanek. B032 is no longer my preferred part, so the recusal question matters only if it returns as an alternative, and I would step back from any decision on it. For B056 and the other candidates no specific conflict is apparent from my profile.
